title: Site transport preserves the canonical Cartesian proper/open interchange
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $p:V\to T$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $i:W\hookrightarrow T$ be an arbitrary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and set $U=V\times_TW$, with projections $k:U\hookrightarrow V$ and $r:U\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the uncompleted unbounded derived operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with exact pro-etale extensions by zero $i_!,k_!$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Assume $p$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and all four schemes are Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. On the small etale sites use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], exact open extensions $i_!^e,k_!^e$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], and write $a_H=\nu_H^*$ for exact comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Let $b_u:a_{\mathrm{target}(u)}Ru^e_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_*a_{\mathrm{source}(u)}$, for $u=p,r$, be the counit-normalized comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Let $e_i:a_Ti_!^e\xrightarrow{\sim}i_!a_W$ and $e_k:a_Vk_!^e\xrightarrow{\sim}k_!a_U$ be the termwise open comparisons [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Let $\Gamma^e:i_!^eRr^e_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp^e_*k_!^e$ be the specified Cartesian comparison [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange]. For $M_0\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ set
$$C_{a_UM_0}=(Rp_*e_k)\circ(b_p k_!^e)\circ(a_T\Gamma^e)\circ(e_i^{-1}Rr^e_*)\circ(i_!b_r^{-1}):i_!Rr_*a_UM_0\longrightarrow Rp_*k_!a_UM_0.$$
This is an isomorphism. For a witness $\alpha:a_UM_0\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], the formula
$$C_M=(Rp_*k_!\alpha)\circ C_{a_UM_0}\circ(i_!Rr_*\alpha^{-1})$$
is independent of witness, natural in $M$, and has the canonical open-adjunction normalization
$$\lambda_M\circ i^*C_M=1_{Rr_*M},\qquad C_M=\varepsilon_i\circ i_!(\lambda_M^{-1}),$$
where $\lambda$ is [lem-exc-proetale-derived-open-restriction] and the adjunction is [prop-exc-open-adjoint]; in the first equation the source $i^*i_!Rr_*M$ of $i^*C_M$ is identified with $Rr_*M$ by the invertible open unit [lem-exc-proetale-open-unit]. All inputs $M$ here are bounded below and of etale origin; no unrestricted ambient exceptional adjoint or all-sheaf finite-CD datum is assumed.

proof.text: The Cartesian base changes preserve the geometric hypotheses needed below. By proper base change, $r:U\to W$ is proper, and by open-immersion base change, $k:U\hookrightarrow V$ is an open immersion. From the definition of properness, $p$ and $r$ are of finite type and separated; finite type gives quasi-compactness, while the diagonal of a separated morphism is a closed immersion and hence quasi-compact, so both maps are qcqs. The exactness of etale and pro-etale extension by zero means that $e_i$ and $e_k$ may be applied termwise to complexes and preserve the derived maps used in the composite.

source.place: Step 7, domain check for the base-changed proper/open square; the proper and open base-change facts are the elementary scheme-theoretic part

proof.text: For $M_0\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, every arrow in the displayed five-arrow composite is an isomorphism. The maps $b_r^{-1}$ and $b_p$ are isomorphisms by the canonical-mate comparison; the maps $e_i$ and $e_k$ are isomorphisms by the canonical etale/pro-etale extension comparison; and $\Gamma^e$ is an isomorphism by the unbounded proper/open interchange. The comparison pullback and the derived direct images are functors, so they preserve these isomorphisms and their composition. Hence $C_{a_UM_0}$ is an isomorphism. Naturality in $M_0$ is the composite of the naturality squares of the five named transformations.

source.place: Step 7, first sentence: the five-arrow site-transport composite; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 099R and more-etale.tex Tag 0F7B

proof.text: Let $(M_0,\alpha)$ be an etale-origin witness for $M$, with $\alpha:a_UM_0\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. The definition of $C_M$ is conjugation of $C_{a_UM_0}$ by $\alpha$, so it is an isomorphism and natural in witnessed maps. If $(M_1,\alpha_1)$ is a second witness, full faithfulness of $\nu_U^*$ on $D^+$ gives a unique isomorphism $\theta:M_0\xrightarrow{\sim}M_1$ with $\alpha_1\circ a_U\theta=\alpha$. Naturality of the five-arrow composite with respect to $\theta$, followed by this equality and cancellation of $Rp_*k_!\alpha_i$ and $i_!Rr_*\alpha_i^{-1}$, identifies the two conjugates. Thus $C_M$ is independent of the witness.

source.place: Step 7, witness independence clause; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 099R

proof.text: Identify the Cartesian square with the comparison-square notation by taking $(f,f',g,g')=(p,r,i,k)$. The canonical pullback comparison is compatible with this Cartesian identification, and the canonical direct-image maps have the counit normalization $\varepsilon^p_{u,A_UK}\circ p_u(b_{u,K})\circ a_{u,r_uK}=A_U(\varepsilon^e_{u,K})$. The transport theorem for the comparison square then states that conjugating the etale unit--square--counit exchange by the pullback comparisons and the normalized $b$-maps gives exactly the pro-etale ambient exchange $\operatorname{Ex}^R$.

source.place: Step 7, comparison coherence in the Cartesian square; the transport identity is the required mate calculation

proof.text: The etale exchange in the preceding step is the same unit--square--counit mate as the unbounded module exchange: [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] defines $\operatorname{Ex}_{p,i}$ by the unit of $i^{-1}\dashv Ri_*$, the Cartesian inverse-image comparison, and the counit of $p^{-1}\dashv Rp_*$. Restricting this formula to the bounded-below etale module input $M_0$ gives the etale exchange used to define $\Gamma^e$; no second exchange map is being substituted.

source.place: Step 7, identification of the etale exchange with the unbounded exchange used in the normalization of $\Gamma^e$

proof.text: For each open edge, apply the unit-normalization statement for the canonical etale/pro-etale extension comparison. For $j=i$ and $j=k$ it gives, termwise and hence on the displayed complexes, $s(c_F)\circ a_{eF}\circ C(\eta^e_F)=\eta^d_{C F}$; thus $e_i$ and $e_k$ intertwine the etale and pro-etale open-adjunction units. Their naturality and composition compatibility are also the stated properties of the extension comparison, and exactness from Step 1 permits the termwise passage. This supplies the unit/counit compatibility required when the five arrows are transposed.

source.place: Step 7, open-comparison unit and counit coherence in the mate-pasting calculation

proof.text: First identify the current restriction normalization with the exchange used in Steps 4--5. For $L=k_!a_UM_0$ choose a K-injective representative $I$. The restriction lemma identifies $\rho_L$ with $i^*p_*I=r_*k^*I$ and states that $k^*I$ is K-injective. Transposing this identification under $r^*\dashv Rr_*$ gives $r^*i^*p_*I\cong k^*p^*p_*I\xrightarrow{k^*\varepsilon_p}k^*I$: the counit evaluates a section after pullback, and both section maps use the same fibre product. This is precisely the defining transpose of the ambient exchange. Thus the current $\lambda_{a_UM_0}$ is that exchange followed by the inverse open unit. Now take the $i_!\dashv i^*$-transpose of the five-arrow map. Insert the open-unit equations from Step 6 at both open edges, the counit equations for $b_r,b_p$ from Step 4, and the Cartesian pullback comparison. The middle square becomes the etale exchange of Step 5, transported to the ambient exchange by Step 4. The normalization clause of $\Gamma^e$ therefore identifies the transpose with $\lambda_{a_UM_0}^{-1}$.

source.place: Step 7, mate-pasting normalization; Stacks more-etale.tex Tag 0F7B

proof.text: The open-adjunction transpose is unique, giving $C_{a_UM_0}=\varepsilon_i\circ i_!(\lambda_{a_UM_0}^{-1})$. Conjugate by a witness $\alpha:a_UM_0\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. Naturality of $\lambda$ and the adjunction counit then gives $$C_M=\varepsilon_i\circ i_!(\lambda_M^{-1}).$$ Applying $i^*$ and the triangle identity gives $$\lambda_M\circ i^*C_M=1_{Rr_*M}.$$

source.place: Step 7, final open-adjunction transpose and triangle-identity clause

proof.text: All constructions remain on the stated ordinary constant-$A$ module categories. The witness supplies $M_0\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, while the comparison, open extension, restriction, and direct-image operations are the ordinary uncompleted pro-etale operations. Therefore the only input restriction is bounded-below etale origin; no ambient exceptional adjoint, constructibility condition, or finite-cohomological-dimension bound is used.
